title: Shipment record
html:
Artworks in a museum move all the time: from storage to a gallery, to the workshop, or out of the building on loan to another museum. A painting never travels loose. It goes in a padded wooden transport crate, like the ones on the trolleys in stage 4.

For every crate the museum keeps a shipment record: which artwork is inside, where the crate has to go, and every step on the way. Staff fill it in at their workstation. A scanner adds a step when the crate passes a door.

A crate can be sent to four places. Each has an ID:

IDPlaceWhat it is
D-01Conservation storageA closed room inside the museum, kept at the right temperature, where artworks stay when they are not on display.
D-02Exhibition preparationThe workshop where artworks are checked and framed before they go on display.
D-03External loading dockThe big door at the back where trucks load and unload: LD on the floor plan, next to the street. A crate sent here leaves the building. A transport company, the carrier, picks it up.
D-04Gallery installationA gallery, where the artwork goes on display.

That afternoon a shipment record was made for crate CR-017: the Mona Lisa would travel in it after the event. At 20:35:12, during the speeches, workstation WS-02 changed that record. Find out what it changed.

The shipment records are not in your files. They are in the museum's collection system, and you can ask for them through its API: a web address that returns data instead of a page. You open it in your browser like any other address.

Try it with the other crate from the corridor, CR-012:

[[api]]shipments/CR-012.json

You get the record of CR-012 as JSON. original_destination is where the crate had to go when the record was made, current_destination is where it has to go now, and events lists every step, oldest first.

Now change CR-012 at the end of the address into the ID of the crate under the cloth.

The API has a documentation page that lists all the addresses you can use: documentation of the museum API.

prev_card.title: You caught the wrong clock
prev_card.html:
Corrected by 7 minutes, the covered crate passed at 20:47:08, ten seconds after Julien Moreau's badge opened the corridor door (20:46:58). Not Thomas Lefebvre. And CAM-04 recorded nothing from 20:41:08 to 20:58:40: WS-02 had switched it off.

This is data quality: the stills were real, but their time was 7 minutes off, and that pointed at the wrong person. The note that corrected it was one sentence in a text file.

hints: Open the example address, then change only its last part: CR-012 becomes the ID on the sticker of the covered crate in stage 4.
In the record, read original_destination and current_destination. For the time: in the events list, the step with the status departed is the moment the crate went out through the door.
D-01, conservation storage. D-03, the external loading dock. The crate left at 20:52:10.
